cites.quote: The patient page shows a `Visit summary` above the appointments list.
The Visit summary shows the number of the patient's `Completed` appointments.
The Visit summary shows the number of the patient's `No-show` appointments.
`Scheduled and Cancelled` appointments are not counted in either number.
A patient with no Completed or No-show appointments shows `0 for each`.
Both counts cover `All time`: every Completed and No-show appointment of the patient, with no period picker.
The patient page's appointments list is `unchanged`.
The patient page's `medical history` is unchanged.
`The rest of the patient page` is unchanged apart from the new Visit summary.
The patient page already lists the patient's appointments, `upcoming first, then past`.
A past appointment the patient did not attend, closed instead of staying Scheduled.
A run of whole hospital-local days ending today: Today, Last 7 days or Last 30 days.
A past appointment the patient did not attend, closed instead of staying Scheduled.
Given a patient with 1 Completed appointment, 1 Scheduled appointment and 1 Cancelled appointment, where the Cancelled one is the most recent

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-2 AC: a patient with 1 Completed appointment and 1 Scheduled appointment whose start time has passed but was never closed. Then: Completed count 1, No-show count 0.
findings.text: No AC has a past appointment that is still Scheduled. A version that counts by date (past and not Cancelled = Completed or No-show) instead of by closed status passes every AC. The glossary says a No-show is closed rather than left Scheduled.

cites.quote: The Visit summary shows the number of the patient's `Completed` appointments.
Given a patient with 2 Completed appointments and 1 No-show appointment, when staff open the patient page

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-1 AC: patient A has 1 Completed appointment and patient B has 2 Completed and 1 No-show. Then patient A's page shows Completed 1 and No-show 0.
findings.text: Every AC sets up a single patient. A count missing the patient filter (all Completed/No-show appointments in the system) passes on a test database with one patient. REQ-2 and REQ-3 require only the patient's own appointments to be counted.

cites.quote: Given a patient with medical history recorded, when staff open the patient page, then the medical history shows the same fields and values as before the change.
The patient page's `medical history` is unchanged.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-3 AC: Given a patient with no medical history recorded, when staff open the patient page, then the medical history area shows the same content as before the change.
findings.text: REQ-8 (medical history unchanged) is tested only for a patient whose history is recorded. The partition with no medical history is missing, although the rubric asks for each partition of an unchanged requirement.

rubric_items.reason: All nine known REQs are traced: S-1 covers REQ-1/2/3/6, S-2 covers REQ-4/5 and S-3 covers REQ-7/8/9. The intent has no assumed REQs.
Each story has one outcome, but S-1 bundles placement, two counts and the counting window. That is acceptable and each part has its own AC.

The ACs are Given/When/Then and checkable. Three gaps: no past still-Scheduled appointment (date-based counting passes), no other patient's appointments (an unscoped count passes) and no patient without medical history.
Every value comes from the intent or the cited glossary Period (Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days). The 2 January 2025 date is only an example and its reason is given inline.
Status names, the Visit summary and the patient page are named the same way throughout and match the glossary. The front matter and the body agree.
